generation.directive: Write absolutely everything in English: the scene text, every line of dialogue, the names of places, objects and characters, and every field of your JSON answer. No French, no other language — except the `visual` fragments, which are explicitly asked for in English anyway.

agreement.masculin: masculine — refer to the player as « he/him » whenever a pronoun is needed, and use masculine nouns (barman, sir) when someone addresses him
agreement.feminin: feminine — refer to the player as « she/her » whenever a pronoun is needed, and use feminine nouns (barmaid, ma'am) when someone addresses her
agreement.neutre: neutral — refer to the player as « they/them », and avoid gendered nouns and forms of address entirely

generation.naming_form: The naming forms given above are French. Keep their INTENT, not their articles: an English place name takes « The Drowned Street », « The Underpass », « The Neon of … », « … Corner », never a literal translation of a French article.
generation.caps_note: The Title Case rule applies as written: English common nouns are lowercase, so a capital stays a clear signal. Capitalise every significant word of an interactive name, keep « the », « of », « to » lowercase inside it.
generation.vocabulary:
IMPOSED LEXICON — the world is cyberpunk, not medieval.
The way out is an AIRLOCK. Never write « door », « gate », « threshold » or « portal »: it is an airlock, and that exact word must appear in the « Exits: » line and in the action verb.
Likewise: a bar or a counter, never an inn or a tavern; neon, screens and tubes, never torches, lanterns or candles; a bartender, never an innkeeper; cables and structures, never beams.
generation.address: Address the player as « you », second person singular, plain and direct — never formal or archaic.

ui.lang.label: Language
ui.lang.hint: The whole night will be written in this language: the story, the characters, and what you type.
ui.login.tagline_line2: towards a resolution that belongs to you.
ui.login.dossier_known: The bureau already has your file
ui.login.dossier_named: In the name of {{name}} — nothing to fill in, the city is waiting.
ui.login.disclaimer_1: The admission form is used only to generate your personalised adventure — characters, places, quest. No account, no social network, no third party.
ui.login.disclaimer_2: Your answers are not recorded on any server: we do not store them, share them or sell them.
ui.login.disclaimer_3: They stay on this device, in your browser, for the length of your adventure — {{days}} days — so that you can pick it up where you left it.
ui.login.disclaimer_4: Starting over below, or clearing this site's data, erases them along with it.

ui.admission.step2_legend: Where you come from, where you sleep.
ui.admission.step3_legend: What you care about, off duty.

ui.admission.step6_legend: The service records how you spend your nights.

ui.admission.last_name_ph: the one you were left with
ui.admission.birthday_hint: The bureau checks the day; the hour is of no interest.
ui.admission.agreement_hint: We will write to you as « {{example}} ».

ui.admission.current_city_ph: the one you come back to at night
ui.admission.current_city_hint: The city of the night will hold on to it: streets, rain, habits.
ui.admission.passions_intro: Three lines, and the order matters: the first weighs heaviest on your night. Write them the way you would say them — an object, a place, an hour beat a category.
ui.admission.passion_ph1: my father's records, which I never dare play
ui.admission.passion_ph3: the bread I've been failing at for two years
ui.admission.anthem_title_ph: the one you put on again
ui.admission.anthem_hint: We will not quote it. We will use it for what is heard behind a door.
ui.admission.turning_intro: Optional, but this is what gives the night something to recognise you by. One line is enough: a departure, a break-up, a job dropped, a city left behind.
ui.admission.keepsake: An object you hold on to
ui.admission.keepsake_ph: the one you will not throw away
ui.admission.refuge: Where you go when things go wrong
ui.admission.refuge_ph: a bar, a quay, a room
ui.admission.ally_ph: we will ask nothing more of you
ui.admission.nights_intro: Everyone has them. It is the ones spent outside that interest us: there is no wrong answer, only undeclared hours.
ui.admission.awake: The nights you do not sleep
ui.admission.awake_ph: at three in the morning, where are you, and what are you doing
ui.admission.awake_hint: Outside, preferably: a quay, a last bar, a walk home. A bedroom ceiling gives the city nothing to build with.
ui.admission.dream_ph: the one you have again, not the latest one
ui.admission.dream_hint: The one that RETURNS: the night can set it down in front of you without repeating itself. If none comes back, leave the line empty.
ui.admission.required_hint: First name and date of birth are required. The rest is not.
ui.verdict.title: Admitted
ui.verdict.p1: Your file went before the night commission. Eleven thousand applications this week; fourteen accepted. Yours is one of them.
ui.verdict.p2: This is not chance: the city only lets in those whose name rings true. Yours was weighed, checked, accepted. What you declared here, the night will use — your cities, your attachments, what you left behind, and how you spend your nights.
ui.verdict.p3_strong: A temporary right of passage is granted to you.
ui.verdict.p3_rest: Report to the bar at the far end of the night. You are expected already, and the rain is not going to stop.

story: You wear it {{item_worn}}. It does not replace your eye: it completes it. Your eye tunes itself to people until it recognises them; this one opens the names of things, which answer to no one.
And reading is not the point: {{item_action}}

story_fallbacks.item_why: Outside, nothing carries a readable name. With this, it does.
story_fallbacks.item_description: A dull, lukewarm lens, heavier than it looks.
story_fallbacks.item_action: that is what a name, once read, will let you do, and could not do before.

howto_pointer: Pick the lens from the toolbar at the top of the scene. The cursor changes shape: that is what you are holding.
Move over a scrambled object name and STOP on it. After a moment, the analysis opens.
Switch back to the eye to read people's names: the two do not read the same thing.
howto_gyro: Pick the lens from the toolbar at the top of the scene.
Tilt the device to bring the eye onto a scrambled object name, and HOLD IT STILL there. After a moment, the analysis opens.
Switch back to the eye to read people's names: the two do not read the same thing.
augmentation_primer.footer: A name you have read does not remember itself. The game will not remember it for you.

body: This button switches on the eye. It reads people's names: bring it onto one of them, and the name deciphers itself.
Everyone here has their own note, and you hear it the moment you recognise them. Turn the sound on.

paywall.gate_text:
Your hand closes on the steel handle of the airlock. The metal is cold. Behind it, {{quest_artifact}} is waiting for you somewhere under the rain.

The airlock does not open yet.

points.label: This world is yours
points.text: The place, the people, the quest: all of it was built from what you have lived. Nothing is generic, nothing will be played again for someone else.

points.label: The quest is not decorative
points.text: {{quest_title}} stages a tension you genuinely carry — the one between what you are and what is expected of you. The game never names it for you. It makes you walk through it.

points.label: The way out matters
points.text: What waits for you outside is not one more level. The way this tension unknots here throws light on the way it can resolve in your life.

pitch.closing: {{quest_artifact}} is waiting for you somewhere under the rain. What you do with it is yours.

messages.scenes: You already have your world. Step through the airlock to see what follows.
messages.turns: The night ends here for you. The airlock is still there.
messages.images: This room already has a face.

messages.scenes: You have travelled a great deal this month. The world needs to breathe.
messages.turns: It has been a long night. Come back tomorrow.
messages.images: Nothing left to draw for now.

lock.message: The city is recharging. Come back when it has finished.
lock.completed_message: This story went all the way. It does not play twice.
